name: Tinder
tagline: Swipe-based dating app with paid tiers for extra likes, boosts and visibility.

pricing.basis: monthly per account, tiered by region and age
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The swipe interface is a weekend of work at most: a card stack, a like table, a mutual-match check, a chat thread. None of that is the product. The product is that tens of millions of people in your metro area already installed it and keep opening it, which is a thing you cannot write in TypeScript. A self-hosted Tinder with three users is not a cheaper Tinder, it is an empty room with very nice lighting. Build it only if you already have a captive crowd, a friend group, a conference, a campus, and even then you inherit moderation, abuse reports and the safety obligations that come with strangers meeting strangers.
coreLoopDIY: A private invite-only swipe deck for a closed group: profiles, photos, like and pass, mutual matches unlock a simple chat.
requirements: A closed group of real users who agree to join, otherwise the app is empty
A server with disk for photo uploads
Someone willing to be the moderator and handle reports
A hosted URL, since nobody will sideload an app to go on dates
whatYouLose: The dating pool, which is the entire value
Mobile apps, push notifications and the muscle memory of opening the app in line at a coffee shop
Geolocation matching at any meaningful density
Trust and safety: photo verification, block and report tooling, ban evasion detection
Any protection against the first bad actor ruining it for everyone
moatNotes: Two-sided liquidity with a geographic constraint, which is the hardest kind: you do not need users, you need users within twelve miles of these users.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay Tinder because the alternative is not another app, it is nobody. The subscription tiers sell attention inside a pool that already exists: more likes, more visibility, seeing who liked you. That pricing only works because the pool is there, and the pool is there because it has been there for over a decade and everyone's friends are on it too. No amount of code reproduces that, and the paid features are deliberately the least interesting part of the system to clone.
notes: The swipe deck is a weekend; the people are not. The moat is geographic liquidity, millions of active accounts within driving distance of each other, plus the trust and safety apparatus that keeps it usable.
prompt:
Build a private, invite-only swipe matching app for a closed group. This is a consolation build, not a Tinder clone: there is no discovery, no public signup, no growth loop.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/app.db
- Photo uploads written to ./data/uploads, served through a route handler
- Session cookies signed with a secret from .env, no third-party auth

In scope:
- Invite codes: an admin CLI script that mints single-use codes; signup requires one
- Profile: display name, age, short bio, up to 4 photos, one free-text prompt answer
- Deck: server returns unseen profiles in random order, excluding self and passed users
- Swipe UI: full-bleed card, like and pass buttons, keyboard arrows, optimistic advance
- Likes table with a unique constraint on (from_user, to_user); on insert, check for the reverse row and create a match
- Matches list and a per-match chat: plain text messages, polling every 5 seconds, no typing indicators
- Block and report: blocking hides both directions immediately; reports land in an admin table
- Admin page gated by an env-set admin email: view reports, ban a user, revoke invites

Out of scope, do not build:
- Geolocation, distance filters, boosts, super likes, any paid tier
- Push notifications, native apps, email sending
- Recommendation ranking, machine learning, photo verification
- Analytics, telemetry, error reporting of any kind

Requirements:
- All secrets in .env, ship a .env.example, never commit data/
- Rate limit likes and messages per user per minute in SQLite, cheaply
- Strip EXIF from uploaded photos and cap them at 5MB, resize to max 1600px
- Seed script that creates 12 fake profiles with placeholder images so the deck is not empty in dev
- README stating plainly that this app is worthless without a pre-existing group of willing users, and that running a service where strangers meet strangers carries moderation and legal obligations you are now responsible for
